summary: The club's first league title, six years after the Newton Heath rescue and still playing at Bank Street, Clayton. Mangnall's side had been assembled cheaply from the Manchester City players banned over illegal payments — Billy Meredith, Sandy Turnbull, Herbert Burgess and Jimmy Bannister — and ran away with the championship by nine points. Turnbull's 25 goals were the division's most.

matches.note: Second game of the season and the one that announced the new side; United won their first ten.

summary: The first FA Cup. United beat Brighton, Everton, Blackburn, Burnley and Newcastle on the way to the final at Crystal Palace, where Sandy Turnbull scored the only goal against Bristol City after a Harold Halse shot hit the bar. The same season the club also won the first Charity Shield (1908) and began building Old Trafford, which opened in February 1910.

matches.note: Both sides wore change strips — United in white with a red V. Turnbull followed up when Halse's shot came back off the bar.

summary: The first title won at Old Trafford, settled on the last afternoon. United needed to beat Sunderland and hope Villa slipped at Liverpool; they won 5–1 and Villa lost 3–1. Mangnall left for Manchester City the following year, and it would be 41 years before the next championship.

matches.note: Final day. Word of Villa's defeat at Anfield reached the ground before the end.

summary: Busby's first trophy, three years after he took the job, and still playing home games at Maine Road while Old Trafford was rebuilt after the bombing. Every round was drawn away or at a neutral ground, with 3–0 wins over Aston Villa (after 6–4 in the third round), Liverpool, Charlton, Preston and Derby. The final against Blackpool is still spoken of as one of Wembley's best: 2–1 down with twenty minutes left, United scored three.

matches.note: Blackpool, with Matthews and Mortensen, led twice. Rowley's second, a header from Morris's free-kick, turned it.
Villa scored inside a minute; United were 5–1 up by half-time.

league: 1st, 57 pts, 4 clear of Tottenham and Arsenal
summary: Four times runners-up in five years, Busby's first great side finally took the title in Carey's last season. It came down to the final day against Arsenal at Old Trafford, who needed to win 7–0 to overhaul United's goal average; United won 6–1. Rowley scored a hat-trick and finished with 30 league goals. Roger Byrne, 22, played the run-in at outside-left — the first of the Babes.

matches.note: Arsenal finished with nine fit men. Carey lifted the trophy a week later in his final home match.

summary: The Busby Babes' first title, won with the youngest side the division had seen — average age 22 — by an eleven-point margin that stood as a record for decades. Duncan Edwards was 19, Eddie Colman 19, Byrne the senior man at 26. The championship was clinched with two games to spare against Blackpool, the only side still in range.

matches.note: 62,277 saw the title clinched. Blackpool led inside two minutes; Taylor's winner came five minutes from time.

summary: Retained with eight points to spare, and the first English side to enter the European Cup against the League's wishes — Anderlecht were beaten 10–0 at Maine Road in September and Real Madrid ended the run in the semi-final. The Double was lost only at Wembley, where goalkeeper Ray Wood's cheekbone was broken after six minutes against Aston Villa and Jackie Blanchflower went in goal.

matches.note: The title clinched. This was the last championship the full Babes side would play for.
Still the club's record win. Old Trafford had no floodlights yet.

summary: Five years after Munich, the first trophy of the rebuilt side — and in a season the league form nearly took United down. Law, bought from Torino for a British record £115,000, scored in the final against Leicester, who had finished fourth and were favourites. David Herd got the other two. It was the beginning of the Law–Charlton–Best side; Best made his debut that September.

matches.note: Law's turn and shot for the first is the goal the day is remembered for; Pat Crerand ran the midfield.

league: 1st, 61 pts, level with Leeds, won on goal average
summary: The first title since Munich, taken from Leeds on goal average after both finished on 61 points — the closest finish the division had seen. Law scored 28 in the league and 39 in all competitions and was named European Footballer of the Year; Best, 18, played every league game. The decisive stretch was April: Leeds beaten 1–0 at Elland Road, then seven straight wins.

matches.note: The title was secured here while Leeds drew at Birmingham. United lost the last game at Villa Park 2–1 and still finished top on goal average.
The head-to-head that settled the race.

summary: Busby's fifth and last title, unbeaten at home all season and sealed with a 6–1 win at West Ham on the penultimate Saturday. It put United back into the European Cup, which is what the season was really for. Alex Stepney, signed from Chelsea in September for £55,000, was the final piece.

matches.note: Title clinched with a game to spare; United were 4–0 up in 25 minutes.

summary: Ten years and three months after Munich, the European Cup. Hibernians of Malta, Sarajevo and Górnik Zabrze were beaten, then Real Madrid in the semi-final: 1–0 at Old Trafford, 3–1 down in the Bernabéu at half-time, then Sadler and Bill Foulkes — Munich survivor, centre-half — scored to go through 4–3. The final at Wembley was 1–1 after 90 minutes against Benfica and Eusébio; United scored three in the first eight minutes of extra time. Best won the Ballon d'Or; Busby was knighted.

matches.note: Stepney's save from Eusébio in the last minute of normal time kept it level. Kidd scored on his 19th birthday. First English winners.
matches.lineup: Stepney; Brennan, Dunne; Crerand, Foulkes, Stiles; Best, Kidd, Charlton, Sadler, Aston

matches.scorers: Sadler 73, Foulkes 78; Pirri 32, Gento 41, Amancio 45 (Zoco og 42)
matches.note: 3–1 down on the night at half-time, 3–2 behind on aggregate; Busby told them they were only one goal away.

summary: The trophy that stopped Liverpool's treble. Docherty's young wing-heavy side had lost the previous year's final to Southampton; this time they beat the league champions and European Cup finalists with two goals in five second-half minutes, Jimmy Greenhoff's winner deflecting in off his chest from Lou Macari's shot. Docherty was sacked six weeks later.

matches.note: Liverpool won the European Cup four days later in Rome.
matches.lineup: Stepney; Nicholl, Albiston; McIlroy, B. Greenhoff, Buchan; Coppell, J. Greenhoff, Pearson, Macari, Hill (McCreery)

summary: Atkinson's first trophy, after losing the League Cup final to Liverpool in March. Brighton, already relegated, drew the final 2–2 — Gordon Smith's miss in the last minute of extra time became a radio catchphrase — and United won the replay 4–0 five days later with two from Robson. Norman Whiteside, 18, scored in both the League Cup and FA Cup finals that season.

matches.note: Robson declined the penalty that would have given him a hat-trick and handed it to Muhren.
matches.lineup: Bailey; Duxbury, Albiston; Wilkins, Moran, McQueen; Robson, Muhren, Stapleton, Whiteside, Davies

matches.note: 'And Smith must score…' — he didn't; Bailey saved with his legs.

summary: Won with ten men. Kevin Moran became the first player sent off in an FA Cup final, for a foul on Peter Reid with twelve minutes left; Everton, league champions and Cup Winners' Cup winners that week, were going for a treble. Whiteside's curling winner from the right in the 110th minute decided it. Hughes, 21, and Robson were the season's players; Hughes was PFA Young Player of the Year.

matches.note: Moran was initially refused a medal; the FA relented.
matches.lineup: Bailey; Gidman, Albiston (Duxbury); Whiteside, McGrath, Moran; Robson, Strachan, Hughes, Stapleton, Olsen

summary: The one that kept Ferguson in the job, or so the story goes: United finished 13th and had been out of the top half most of the season. Mark Robins' header at Forest in the third round started a run of away draws all the way to Wembley. The final against Crystal Palace was 3–3, Hughes equalising in extra time; Ferguson dropped Jim Leighton for the replay and Les Sealey kept a clean sheet as Lee Martin's goal won it.

matches.note: Ferguson's first trophy at United, three and a half years after arriving.
matches.lineup: Sealey; Ince, Martin; Bruce, Phelan, Pallister; Robson, Webb, McClair, Hughes, Wallace

matches.note: Ian Wright came off the bench with a broken leg barely healed and scored twice.
The goal usually credited with saving Ferguson's job.

summary: English clubs were back in Europe after the five-year ban and United won the Cup Winners' Cup at the first attempt, beating Pécsi Munkás, Wrexham, Montpellier and Legia Warsaw, then Johan Cruyff's Barcelona in Rotterdam. Hughes, sold by Barcelona five years earlier, scored both. Lee Sharpe, 19, was PFA Young Player of the Year; the League Cup final was lost to Sheffield Wednesday.

matches.note: Hughes's second came from a narrow angle after rounding Busquets. Clayton Blackmore cleared off the line late on.
matches.lineup: Sealey; Irwin, Blackmore; Bruce, Pallister, Phelan; Robson, Ince, McClair, Hughes, Sharpe

summary: The season the title slipped — top in April, then four games in eight days and Leeds went past — but two cups came in. Red Star Belgrade, European champions, were beaten 1–0 in the Super Cup at Old Trafford in November, and McClair's goal won the first League Cup against Nottingham Forest in April. Peter Schmeichel arrived in the summer; Ryan Giggs, 18, was PFA Young Player of the Year.

matches.note: Giggs set it up. Forest had beaten United in the 1990 FA Cup quarter and the 1991 League Cup; this was the first final between the clubs.
matches.lineup: Schmeichel; Parker, Irwin; Bruce, Pallister, Kanchelskis (Sharpe); Giggs, Ince, McClair, Hughes, Phelan

matches.note: Single leg because of the war in Yugoslavia.

summary: The first title in 26 years and the first of the Premier League. United were tenth in November when Eric Cantona arrived from Leeds for £1.2m; they lost twice in the remaining 28 league games. The pivot was 10 April against Sheffield Wednesday: 1–0 down with four minutes left, Bruce headed two, the second in the seventh minute of stoppage time, and Ferguson and Brian Kidd ended up on the pitch. The title was confirmed on 2 May when Villa lost to Oldham; United beat Blackburn the next night and lifted the trophy.

matches.note: Referee Michael Peck pulled a muscle and linesman John Hilditch took over, which is why seven minutes were added. 'Fergie time' was born here.
The night the trophy was presented; Pallister's free-kick was his first goal of the season.

summary: The first Double, and nearly a treble — the League Cup final was lost to Aston Villa in March. Roy Keane came from Forest for a British record £3.75m; Cantona was Footballer of the Year. United led the league from August, saw a 16-point gap shrink to three as Blackburn chased, then won six of the last seven. The FA Cup final was 4–0 against Chelsea, who had beaten United twice in the league, with Cantona scoring two penalties in the rain.

matches.note: Goalless and under pressure at half-time; three goals in nine minutes after the break.
matches.lineup: Schmeichel; Parker, Irwin (Sharpe); Bruce, Pallister, Kanchelskis (McClair); Keane, Ince, Cantona, Hughes, Giggs

matches.note: Three days after Hughes's volley in the 119th minute had saved the first match at Wembley.
The next day Blackburn lost at Coventry and the title was retained.

summary: 'You can't win anything with kids.' Ince, Hughes and Kanchelskis were sold in the summer; Beckham, Scholes, Butt, Gary Neville and Phil Neville came in, and United lost the opening day at Villa Park. Newcastle were 12 points clear in January; Cantona, back from his eight-month ban, scored the only goal in six of United's wins in the spring, including at St James' Park. The title was sealed 3–0 at Middlesbrough on the last day, and Cantona's late volley beat Liverpool in the final for a second Double.

matches.note: James punched a corner out; Cantona, adjusting his body on the edge of the box, volleyed through the crowd. Liverpool's white suits are the other memory.
matches.lineup: Schmeichel; Irwin, P. Neville; May, Pallister, Keane; Beckham (G. Neville), Butt, Cantona, Cole (Scholes), Giggs

matches.note: Schmeichel's first half kept Newcastle out; the gap went to one point.
Final day. Keegan's 'I'd love it' interview had been a week earlier.

summary: A fourth title in five years, won with the lowest points total of Ferguson's championships and a European Cup semi-final lost to Borussia Dortmund. Solskjær, an unknown £1.5m signing from Molde, finished top scorer; Beckham scored from halfway at Selhurst Park on the opening day and was PFA Young Player of the Year. The title was confirmed on 6 May when Liverpool and Newcastle both failed to win; Cantona retired twelve days later, at 30.

matches.scorers: Keane 36, G. Neville 42, Solskjær 68; Juninho 15, Emerson 50, Hignett 61 (pen)
matches.note: The point that left Liverpool needing to win at Wimbledon the next night. They lost, Newcastle drew, and the title was United's.
The low point — followed by 6–3 at Southampton and a first home European defeat to Fenerbahçe. United still finished seven clear.

summary: The Treble. Thirty-three games unbeaten from Boxing Day to the end of May, every competition decided in the final ten days. The league was won on the last day against Tottenham after going a goal down; the FA Cup final against Newcastle was 2–0, four days after the semi-final replay against Arsenal that Schmeichel's penalty save and Giggs's run had turned; and in Barcelona on 26 May, trailing to Mario Basler's sixth-minute free-kick for 85 minutes, Sheringham and Solskjær scored from two Beckham corners in injury time. Keane's semi-final at Juventus — booked, knowing he would miss the final, and dragging United from 2–0 down to win 3–2 — is the performance Ferguson rated above any other.

matches.note: Keane and Scholes suspended. Bayern hit the woodwork twice through Scholl and Jancker before the two corners. 'Football, bloody hell.'
matches.lineup: Schmeichel; G. Neville, Johnsen, Stam, Irwin; Beckham, Butt, Giggs, Blomqvist (Sheringham 67); Cole (Solskjær 81), Yorke

matches.note: Two down after eleven minutes. Keane's header, then his booking for a foul on Zidane.
Keane sent off, Schmeichel saved Bergkamp's penalty in the last minute, then Giggs took the ball from Vieira in his own half and beat five players.
Keane went off injured after eight minutes; Sheringham replaced him and scored within three.
matches.lineup: Schmeichel; G. Neville, May, Johnsen, P. Neville; Beckham, Scholes (Stam), Keane (Sheringham), Giggs; Cole (Yorke), Solskjær

matches.note: Arsenal beat Villa 1–0 at the same time; one point separated them at the end.

scorer: Dwight Yorke, 20 league, Cole 22 in all
summary: The largest winning margin in Premier League history at the time — 18 points — with eleven straight wins to finish. United did not defend the FA Cup, going to Brazil for the Club World Championship instead, but in November had beaten Palmeiras in Tokyo to be world champions: Keane scored, Mark Bosnich made the saves. The European Cup went at the quarter-final, 3–2 at home to Real Madrid after a 0–0 in the Bernabéu.

matches.note: Giggs's run and cross; Keane at the far post. First British winners.
matches.lineup: Bosnich; G. Neville, Stam, Silvestre, Irwin; Beckham, Butt, Keane, Giggs; Solskjær (Sheringham), Yorke (Scholes)

matches.note: Title clinched with four games left.

summary: Three in a row for the first time in the club's history, with Sheringham, 35, as Footballer of the Year and PFA Player of the Year. The gap was 16 points in March. Arsenal were beaten 6–1 at Old Trafford in February, Yorke scoring a hat-trick in the first 22 minutes; the title arrived on 14 April after Arsenal lost at Middlesbrough and United beat Coventry.

matches.note: Arsenal's heaviest defeat under Wenger at that point.
The title was confirmed an hour before kick-off when Arsenal lost 3–0 at the Riverside.

scorer: Ruud van Nistelrooy, 25 league, 44 in all
summary: Eight points behind Arsenal at the start of March, champions by five. Van Nistelrooy scored in ten consecutive league games at the end of the season and 44 in all; Ferguson had been due to retire the previous summer and changed his mind. The turning point was Arsenal's 2–2 draw at Bolton on 26 April and their loss to Leeds a week later; Beckham played his last United game in the final match and left for Real Madrid that summer.

matches.note: The next day Arsenal lost 3–2 at home to Leeds, and the title was United's.
Out of Europe, but the night Ronaldo was applauded off by Old Trafford and Beckham scored twice from the bench. Included because the season is unexplained without it.

scorer: Ruud van Nistelrooy, 20 league, 30 in all
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's first season and first trophy. Arsenal went the league unbeaten, but United knocked them out of the FA Cup in the semi-final at Villa Park with Scholes's goal, then beat Millwall 3–0 in the first final in Cardiff. Ronaldo, 19, headed the first; Van Nistelrooy scored a penalty and a second. Rio Ferdinand began an eight-month ban in January for a missed drugs test.

matches.note: Millwall were a First Division side managed by Dennis Wise.
matches.lineup: Howard (Carroll); G. Neville, Brown, Silvestre, O'Shea; Ronaldo (Solskjær), Fletcher (Butt), Keane, Scholes, Giggs; Van Nistelrooy

matches.note: The only domestic defeat of Arsenal's Invincibles season.

summary: The Glazer takeover summer, Keane's departure in November after the MUTV interview, out of the Champions League at the group stage for the first time in a decade — and a League Cup won 4–0 against Wigan in Cardiff, with Rooney scoring twice. Van Nistelrooy was left on the bench for the final and left for Madrid in the summer. Edwin van der Sar and Park Ji-sung arrived; the side that would win three straight titles was forming.

matches.note: Three goals in six second-half minutes.
matches.lineup: Van der Sar; G. Neville, Ferdinand, Brown, Silvestre (Evra); Ronaldo, O'Shea, Giggs, Park (Richardson); Saha (Van Nistelrooy), Rooney

summary: The title back after three years of Arsenal and Chelsea. Ronaldo, booed everywhere after the World Cup, won both player-of-the-year awards; Scholes was reborn in a deeper role; Vidić and Evra settled. Roma were beaten 7–1 at Old Trafford in April; Milan ended the European run in the semi-final. The championship came on 6 May when Chelsea drew with Arsenal the day after Ronaldo's penalty beat City at the Etihad.

matches.note: Chelsea's draw the next afternoon confirmed it.

matches.scorers: Carrick 11, 60, Smith 17, Rooney 19, Ronaldo 44, 49, Evra 81; De Rossi 69
matches.note: 4–0 up after 19 minutes.

summary: Ronaldo's 42 goals, the Ballon d'Or, and the Double of league and European Cup, fifty years after Munich. Tevez and Nani and Anderson arrived; the title was won at Wigan on the last day while Chelsea drew with Bolton. The final in Moscow, against Chelsea, was 1–1 after Ronaldo's header and Lampard's equaliser, and went to penalties: Ronaldo missed, John Terry slipped with the cup on his boot, and Van der Sar saved from Anelka.

matches.note: Drogba sent off in extra time for a slap on Vidić. Giggs, on for Scholes, broke Charlton's appearance record and scored the decisive penalty.
matches.lineup: Van der Sar; Brown (Anderson), Ferdinand, Vidić, Evra; Hargreaves, Scholes (Giggs), Carrick; Ronaldo, Rooney (Nani), Tevez

matches.note: Final day; Giggs scored on his 758th appearance, equalling Charlton's record.
A Scholes strike from 25 yards, three years after he had missed the 2005 semi through suspension.

summary: Three in a row for the second time, equalling Liverpool's 18 titles. Van der Sar went 1,311 league minutes without conceding, a record; Berbatov came from Spurs for £30.75m; Rooney, Ronaldo and Tevez shared the goals. The Club World Cup was won in Yokohama in December, the League Cup on penalties against Tottenham in March, the title with a 0–0 against Arsenal in May. The Champions League final in Rome was lost 2–0 to Barcelona, and Ronaldo left for Madrid for £80m.

matches.note: Vidić sent off after 49 minutes; Rooney's winner from Ronaldo's pass with ten men.
matches.lineup: Van der Sar; Rafael (Evra), Ferdinand, Vidić, Evra; Park, Carrick, Anderson (Fletcher), Ronaldo; Rooney, Tevez (Giggs)

matches.note: Ben Foster saved Jamie O'Hara's kick after studying it on an iPod on the touchline; Giggs, Tevez, Ronaldo and Anderson scored.
The point that clinched the 18th title, three days after a 2–0 win at Wigan from 1–0 down.

summary: Rooney's best season as a United player, 34 goals and both player-of-the-year awards, and the League Cup retained against Aston Villa with a late Rooney header from the bench. The title was lost by a point to Chelsea — the 2–1 defeat at Stamford Bridge in April, with Drogba's offside winner, was the hinge — and Bayern went through on away goals in the European quarter-final after Rafael's red card.

matches.note: Owen pulled a hamstring just before half-time; Rooney replaced him and headed the winner from Valencia's cross.

summary: The 19th title, the one that passed Liverpool. Unbeaten at home all season, won only five away before February, and still champions by nine points; Chicharito, £7m from Guadalajara, scored 20; Berbatov shared the Golden Boot. Rooney's overhead kick beat City in February; the title was clinched at Blackburn with his penalty on 14 May. The season ended with Barcelona at Wembley — a 3–1 defeat Ferguson called the best side he had faced.

matches.note: The point that made it 19.
The overhead kick from Nani's deflected cross.

summary: Ferguson's 13th title and his last, a year after the Agüero goal had taken the 2012 championship on goal difference. Van Persie, 29, signed from Arsenal for £24m, scored 26 and won the Golden Boot; the title was clinched with four games left on 22 April with his hat-trick against Aston Villa, the second a volley from Rooney's long pass. Ferguson announced his retirement on 8 May; his last match was a 5–5 at West Brom.

matches.note: The 20th title. The second goal — Rooney's 40-yard pass, Van Persie's first-time volley — was the Premier League's Goal of the Season.
Ferguson's last home match; the trophy presented afterwards. Ferdinand's winner was his first league goal in five years.

summary: The 12th FA Cup, 12 years after the 11th, and Van Gaal's only trophy — he was sacked two days after the final. Martial, 19, scored the stoppage-time winner against Everton in the semi-final; Marcus Rashford, 18, had burst in with two goals on his debut against Midtjylland in February and two more against Arsenal three days later. The final against Crystal Palace went to extra time after Puncheon's goal and Mata's reply; Lingard volleyed the winner with ten men after Smalling's red card.

matches.note: Lingard's volley from the edge of the box, with United down to ten.
De Gea saved Lukaku's penalty; Martial finished a counter in added time.

summary: Two cups in Mourinho's first season, plus the Community Shield; the league was 25 games unbeaten and still only sixth, with 15 draws. Ibrahimović, 35, scored 28, two of them in the League Cup final against Southampton — the winner a header in the 87th minute. Pogba returned for a world-record £89m. The Europa League, the one European trophy United had never won, was taken in Stockholm against Ajax two days after the Manchester Arena bombing: Pogba and Mkhitaryan, and a Champions League place.

matches.note: Pogba's deflected shot, then Mkhitaryan's hooked finish from a corner. United had 31% of the ball and won comfortably.
Southampton had a Gabbiadini goal wrongly disallowed at 0–0 and came back from 2–0 down; Ibrahimović's late header from Herrera's cross.

summary: The first trophy in six years, in Ten Hag's first season. Ronaldo left in November after the Piers Morgan interview; Rashford scored 30; Casemiro arrived from Real Madrid and scored the first goal in the final against Newcastle, Sven Botman's own goal the second. The FA Cup final — the first Manchester derby final — was lost 2–1 to City, who went on to the treble.

matches.note: Casemiro's header from Shaw's free-kick; Rashford's shot deflected in off Botman six minutes later.
The derby that marked the season's high point — and the Rashford offside argument.

league: 8th — the club's lowest Premier League finish
summary: The worst league season since 1990 and the 13th FA Cup, won against Manchester City at Wembley with two first-half goals from academy graduates: Garnacho after Ortega and Gvardiol collided, Mainoo from Fernandes's pass. Doku pulled one back late. It was the second consecutive derby final and the first United had won; Ten Hag kept his job on the strength of it, for five more months.

matches.note: Mainoo, 19, was man of the match. City's attempt at back-to-back trebles ended.

matches.scorers: McTominay 23, Maguire 45+1, Fernandes 58; Simms 71, O'Hare 79, Wright 90+5 (pen)
matches.note: 3–0 up with 20 minutes left; Coventry's extra-time 'winner' ruled out by VAR for offside by a toe.
